head.partly: Partly shipped · {shipped} of {ordered} garments have left
head.delivered: Delivered on {day}: every garment has shipped and every shipment has arrived
head.making_one: {count} is still to be made or released
head.making_other: {count} are still to be made or released
head.back: {number} came back with the carrier: receive the garments in Warehouse, then ship them again
head.backOn: {number} came back with the carrier on {day}: receive the garments in Warehouse, then ship them again

where.title: Where every garment is
where.info: Every garment of this order is in one bucket, and the buckets add up to what was ordered. Nothing here is typed: it is counted, and a number changes only through its cause (a shipment, a release, a line closed).
where.more: More for Where every garment is

answer.back: {count} came back and wait to be received

bucket.making: Still to be made or released

card.gridCaption: {style}: still to ship by colour and size
card.nothingLeft: Nothing of this style is left to ship.
card.nothingOn: Nothing of this style is on a shipment yet.
card.mtm: Made to measure: each unit is one person's garment, so it is counted in units, not by size.

fact.making: Still to be made or released:

state.pending: Waits for a yes: nothing ships yet.

ships.info: Every shipment of this order: what it carries, where it is, how it travels and what comes next. Each step stays in Warehouse, the shipment's home: Next › opens it there. Keys: Tab moves through the rows' links and buttons; Enter opens.

empty.ready_one: No shipment yet: {count} garment is ready now.
empty.ready_other: No shipment yet: {count} garments are ready now.
empty.nothing: No shipment yet: nothing is ready now.
empty.warehouse: No shipment yet. The warehouse makes shipments.

create.hint: Create shipment… opens when a released garment waits on no shipment.

held.making_one: Nothing is ready now: {count} garment is still to be made or released.
held.making_other: Nothing is ready now: {count} garments are still to be made or released.
held.back: Nothing is ready now: the garments that came back are not received yet.
held.planned: Nothing is ready now: every released garment is on a shipment already.

chip.noDdt: Travels without a DDT · Set by hand

next.ddtChoice: A Nexus shipment leaves with a DDT. If the DDT cannot be issued (Warehouse lists its open checks), choose “This shipment travels without a DDT…” in ⋯, then hand it over.

travels.elsewhere: Made elsewhere: no parcels in Nexus
travels.ownVan: Our van: no tracking number; its status is typed in Warehouse.
travels.draft: Parcels get numbers once the shipment is packed.

parcels.label: Parcels of {number}
parcels.nothingIn: Nothing is in this parcel yet.

act.ddtOff: This shipment travels without a DDT…

held.splitPacked: Only a draft can be split: unpack it first.
held.movePacked: Only a draft gives or takes garments: unpack it first.
held.ddtLive: A live DDT names it: annul the DDT first.
held.labelled: A parcel has a carrier label: void the labels first.
held.ddtCarrier: The DDT names the carrier: annul it to change who carries.
held.carrierFed: The carrier's own tracking follows it: nothing to type.
held.proofKept: Every part of the proof is kept: it never changes.
held.received: The garments were received back already.

act.return: Open a return for this shipment…
act.complaint: Log a complaint about this shipment…

done.eta: The expected arrival of {number} is saved.
done.proof: The proof of delivery of {number} is saved.
done.resolve: The tracking problem of {number} is resolved.
done.tracking: The tracking numbers of {number} are saved.

told.draft: The customer is not told: a draft is never shown.
told.portal: The customer is not e-mailed; their portal shows it at once.
told.ddtOff: The customer sees the shipment from Packed on, without a DDT.
told.tracking: The customer sees the numbers in their portal at once; no e-mail.
told.noticeSent: The shipping notice went to the customer again.
told.noticeHeld: The shipping notice did not go; the shipment's Customer notice in Warehouse says why.

after.info: What the customer reported about what we shipped, and where each case stands. The tab only lists a case: each one lives on its own page.

held.return: A return opens once something has shipped.
held.claim: A claim link is sent for a shipment that left.

done.complaintPhotos_one: Complaint {number} is logged; {count} photo could not be added.
done.complaintPhotos_other: Complaint {number} is logged; {count} photos could not be added.

door.officeOnly: Office only: the customer never reads them.
door.customerNotTold: The customer is not told: a draft is never shown.
door.audit: Saved with your name and the time; the history keeps before and after.

held.busy: Wait: the last change is being saved.

takeOff.oneStep: In one step, all or nothing: they go back to what the order can still ship; the other orders on it keep everything.

handOver.whenHint: Only when the goods left before it was recorded: stock and the cost of sales still post now.
handOver.notATime: The time is not a time.
handOver.future: The time is in the future.
handOver.beforePacked: The time is before the goods were packed.
handOver.beforeDdt: The time is before the DDT was issued.
handOver.why: Say why the goods are recorded as handed over at another time (3 to 500 characters).

ddt.title: {number} travels without a DDT
ddt.what: No DDT number is taken (no gap). It is handed over with its parcels and their typed numbers; aggregator labels still need a DDT (book the carrier by hand). The invoice is made by hand in Finance.
ddt.tick: No DDT travels with these goods.
ddt.hint: For an Italian company this is allowed only when an immediate invoice travels with the goods (the same rule as “Record a shipment made elsewhere”).
ddt.told: The customer sees the shipment from Packed on, without a DDT.
ddt.never: A shipment with a live DDT never takes it; only released garments ship; it reads no country.
ddt.backWhat: From now on it leaves only with a DDT again: issue it in Warehouse before the hand-over.

held.elsewhere: A shipment made elsewhere has its own choice.
held.left: The goods have left or it is cancelled: this is decided before they leave.
held.tick: Tick “No DDT travels with these goods.”

refusal.ELSEWHERE: A shipment made elsewhere has its own choice.
refusal.LEFT: The goods have left: this is decided before they leave.
refusal.DDT_LIVE: A live DDT names it: annul the DDT first.
refusal.SAME: Nothing to change: it is so already.

receive.title: Receive the garments of {number} back
receive.what_one: The carrier brought {count} garment back: it goes into finished goods.
receive.what_other: The carrier brought {count} garments back: they go into finished goods.
receive.then: They count in stock again and as still to ship; ship them again with a new shipment.

held.notReturned: Only a shipment the carrier brought back is received.
held.nothing: Nothing of it is left to receive.
held.noPlace: This site has no finished-goods place: an administrator adds one first.

status.why: Say why you know better than the carrier (at least {min} characters).
status.labelled: The carrier's tracking moves this shipment. Mark it only if you know better, and say why: it is tagged “Set by hand”.
status.deliveredFinal: Delivered is final: it never goes back. Payment steps that start on delivery start from this day.
status.returnedThen: The garments count as still to ship again; they wait to be received in Warehouse.
status.told: The customer is not e-mailed; their portal shows it at once.

eta.title: Expected arrival of {number}
eta.what: For a carrier booked by hand or our van: no carrier feed tracks it, so the office types the day.
eta.told: The customer sees the day in their portal.
eta.notADay: The day is not a day.
eta.beforeLeft: The day is before the goods left.

refusal.CARRIER_FED: The carrier's own tracking follows it: nothing to type.
refusal.NOT_LEFT_OR_PACKED: An expected arrival is typed once the goods are packed.
refusal.ARRIVED: It is delivered or came back already: its arrival is known.

done.unpacked: {number} is unpacked: it is a draft again.
done.received: {count} garments of {number} are back in finished goods.

tracking.title: Tracking numbers of {number}
tracking.awbFits: It looks like an air waybill number, and its last digit fits.
tracking.awbOff: It looks like an air waybill number, but its last digit does not fit: check it.
tracking.fromLabel: From the label: its number comes from the carrier.

refusal.PARCEL_LABELLED: This parcel carries a label: its number comes from the label, never typed.
refusal.NOT_PACKED: Parcels get their numbers once the shipment is packed.

tracking.afterLeft: A parcel's typed number may change after the goods left; the customer sees the new one at once.
tracking.fromPacked: From Packed on. A number is typed only on a parcel without a carrier label.
tracking.seen: The customer saw the old number: say why it changes.
tracking.why: Say why the number changes (at least {min} characters).
tracking.parcelTooLong: Parcel {seq}: the number is one line of at most {max} characters.
tracking.parcelLinkNeedsNumber: Parcel {seq}: a link goes only with its number.
tracking.parcelLink: Parcel {seq}: the link starts with https:// and has at most {max} characters.
tracking.notifyHint: Off by default: the customer sees the new numbers in the portal and on the tracking page at once; an e-mail goes only when ticked.
tracking.toldPacked: The customer sees the numbers in their portal; no e-mail from this window.
tracking.never: A number from a carrier label is never typed over. The DDT is not touched. The history keeps every old number; the thread gets one office line.
tracking.doneNotice: The tracking numbers are saved and the shipping notice went again.
tracking.doneNoticeHeld: The tracking numbers are saved; the shipping notice did not go.

split.intoHint: This one and up to {max} new ones, in one step (all or nothing).
split.shipComplete: The customer wants it all in one delivery (ship complete): split only if they agreed.
split.eachTakes: Each new shipment takes at least one garment: give new shipment {n} some, or split into fewer.
split.address: Delivery address of the new shipments
split.noAddress: This customer has no other approved delivery address: add one on the customer first.
split.onlyOwn: Each new shipment shows only on the orders whose garments it carries; the holds in force go with it.

move.title: Move garments of {number} to another draft
move.what: Only drafts of the same customer, company and site take them; both drafts are locked together; the target's holds are checked for every order.
move.mergeWhat_one: All {count} garment of {number} moves; {number} is then cancelled “Merged into …”, never deleted; its holds come along. Undo: Split….
move.mergeWhat_other: All {count} garments of {number} move; {number} is then cancelled “Merged into …”, never deleted; its holds come along. Undo: Split….
move.never: Cartons and serials stay; released counts and the orders' lines never change; nothing is deleted.
move.mergeNever: Released counts and the orders' lines never change; the emptied draft stays, cancelled, with its history.

held.notDraft: Only a draft gives or takes garments: unpack it first.
held.busy: Wait: the move is being made.
held.noTarget: No other draft of this customer can take them: make one with Create shipment…
held.pickTarget: Pick the draft that takes them.
held.useMerge: Nothing stays: use Merge into… instead.

refusal.NOT_DRAFT: Only a draft gives or takes garments.
refusal.OTHER_SITE: That draft waits at another site.
refusal.NOTHING_TO_MOVE: Nothing can move: every garment is in a carton or has a serial.
refusal.NOTHING_STAYS: Nothing stays: use Merge into… instead.
refusal.ON_HOLD_QUALITY: A work order of these garments is on a quality hold.
refusal.MERGE_PACKED: Some garments are in cartons or have serials: take them out of the cartons first.
refusal.MERGE_LABELLED: A parcel has a carrier label: void the labels first.
refusal.NOT_ON_IT: None of this order's garments is on it any more.
refusal.FIRST_ORDER: This shipment was made for this order: move the other orders' garments with Split… or Move garments to…, then cancel it.
refusal.IN_CARTON: A garment of this order is in a carton: take it out first.

claim.title: Send a claim link for {number}
claim.what: The customer gets a link to ask for a return or report a quality problem, with photos. The link is for them only.
claim.noContact: No contact of this customer has an e-mail address here: type one.
claim.never: Nothing else changes: no return or complaint opens until the customer sends one.

refusal.SUPPRESSED: This address bounced or complained: correct it first.
refusal.email: That address cannot take the link: check it.
refusal.notFound: A claim link names a shipment that left or an open order: this one is neither now.
refusal.other: The link could not go: try again in a moment.

sent.queued: The link waits to go to {email}.
sent.failed: The link was made, but the e-mail to {email} failed: send a new one later.
